title: Kiln Dried Sand Applications
excerpt: Applying an infill of kiln dried silica sand on top of artificial or synthetic grass is an essential part of installing it, helping the grass strands stand proud and weighing the grass down flat.
bodyHtml:
Applications for Kiln Dried Sand

Applying an “infill” of sand on the top of Artificial or Synthetic Grass is an essential aspect of installing grass. By applying kiln dried Silica sand on the top of Artificial grass it assists in making the grass strands stand proud and weighing the grass down flat.

The Sand is produced from Quartz rock and is crushed, tumbled, processed and dried removing all moisture content.

As a guide we recommend infilling 1 x 20Kg bag for every 3 square metres (3 m²).

This product is painful to use when it’s raining so choose a clear day to apply it.

The sand grains are well rounded with a grain size within the range of 0.15 – 0.6mm.

Applying the sand to the surface is as easy as hand spreading (like you are feeding the chickens). For larger surfaces or sports fields sand spreaders are used. Once applied a broom can be used to evenly spread the sand into the grass.

  • Kiln dried Silica sand is fine to coarse grains varying in colour from white to yellow
  • Typically, the sand is 30/65 size.
  • At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we also carry 15kg bags of Smellbgone™ infill which is an alternative to sand as an infill that absorbs the pet’s urine odour.
  • Kiln dried sand infill improves the ability of the grass strands to stand upright.
  • Improves the visual aesthetics of the grass.
  • Weighs the grass down, assisting in keeping it “weighed down”

Types of Sand

At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies we carry 5 types of sands:

  • Kiln Dried Silica Sand
  • White Brick Sand
  • Washed Sand (Concrete Sand)
  • Triple Washed Sand
  • Gap Sand

Feel free to call the shop, drop in, instant message or email us if you require any advice.

title: Which Sand should I use?
excerpt: Have you ever asked yourself what type of sand is the best to use for your application? A guide to the four sands we carry at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies and what each is used for.
bodyHtml:
What type of Sand do I use?

Have you ever asked yourself what type of sand is the best to use for my application?

With many projects underway in our surrounding suburbs of Mont Albert, Balwyn North, Blackburn, Camberwell and Kew, Surrey Hills Garden Supplies are ideally located at 682 Canterbury Rd Surrey Hills to supply all of your sand requirements for your job site or project.

At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we carry 4 types of sand.

Our White Brick Sand is very popular with many brick layers as it is very consistent with its content of clay and has a high “fatty” content which in turn makes it easier to work with and less lime additive is required.

Our Packing sand is a high-quality sand that is primarily used for underneath concrete slabs. Due to its high content of clay it holds its shape well.

Our Washed Sand is also a high quality sand sourced locally and has several applications but the main uses are for creating concrete. It is also used for paving and plastering. It’s a coarse sand and size is typically 0.06 to 2mm.

Our Triple Washed Sand also has a variety of uses. The most common is for tiling, grouting and shower bases. Its typical size is less than 1.5mm. It is also commonly used in children’s sandpits and playgrounds.

Our Kiln Dried Sand is the finest sand carried at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies and has no moisture content. The most common application is for infill for Artificial turf. We carry it in 20kg bags and 1 tonne bulker bags.

In addition to our sands at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we carry aggregate rocks and cement for producing concrete. 4 types of cement: General Purpose (GP), Builders Cement, Off White Cement and Mortar. All in 20kg bags.

No need to leave home or the work site as we deliver as little as 1/8 (0.125) of a cubic metre up to a full large truck full of product. We offer delivery to all surrounding suburbs such as Box Hill, Canterbury, Glen Iris, Burwood and Balwyn. As a rough guide 1/8 (0.125) of a cubic metre is a large barrow worth of product. An average trailer (6 x 4) would hold ¾ of a cubic metre (0.75).

If you would like help planning and calculating your sand requirements feel free to contact us at the shop on 9890 3901 or utilise our helpful volume calculator on our website.

We are here to help you with your project,

title: Which Mulch should I use around my home?
excerpt: Have you ever asked yourself which mulch (ground covering) is the best to use? We compare Black Midnight Mulch, 10mm and 20mm Pine Bark and Organic Mulch for garden beds around your home.
bodyHtml:
Which Mulch do I use around my home?

Have you ever asked yourself which mulch (ground covering) is the best to use?

In these uncertain times of Covid19 with many restrictions in place you are still able to order over the phone with Surrey Hills Garden Supplies mulches for your gardens. All contactless!

In our local suburbs such as Balwyn North, Blackburn, Canterbury and Kew, large yards are common and there is a fair bit of mulch required to cover a garden bed.

At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we carry 4 types of mulches in the bulk bins and we also carry bales of pea straw and red mulch in 60 litre bags.

Our Black Midnight Mulch is produced from recycled timber. The Longalife® coloured mulches have the added bonus of retaining colour for a substantially longer period than traditional mulches. It is recommended that coloured mulches are turned over with a shovel or pitchfork every 6 weeks. The Black Midnight Mulch is purely a decorative mulch and has no fertilising or organic properties.

Our 10mm Pine Bark is chocolatey-brown nuggets in appearance. It’s also known as Cottage Bark or Tan Bark. It’s renowned for its ability not to blow or wash away, but still allows airflow to the soil, as well as being excellent at water retention. It is long lasting and has good capacity to absorb and retain moisture. Installation should be to a depth of 100mm for new applications and typically 50-75mm for “top up” installations.

Our 20mm Pine Bark is a larger version of the Pine Bark and brown in appearance. 20mm Pine is generally used to cover larger open areas or larger garden beds. It’s also known as Tan Bark. It is long lasting, has good capacity to absorb and retain moisture, and is also extremely low maintenance. Installation should be to a depth of 100mm for new applications and typically 50-75mm for “top up” installations.

Our ever popular Organic Mulch is an organic product. It’s also known as Compost or Compost Mulch. Organic Mulch is dark grey to almost black in appearance when moist. The blend comprises of soft garden organics, leaves and small branches that are mulched and aged until mature. Aged super fines, aged saw dust and Urea (nitrogen based additive) are also added to the blend. Organic Mulch is great for increasing the level of organic matter for any type of soil, which in turn improves moisture retention, reduces soil erosion and gives slow release of nutrients into the soil. Organic Mulch creates an ideal environment for worms and micro-organisms.

In addition to our mulches at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, you can also enhance gardens by adding products such as fertilisers. We carry 4 types of manure – cow manure, sheep manure, poultry manure and Dynamic Lifter – as well as grass seed, grass fertilisers and Charlie Carp. Other products that are used in vegie patches that we carry are Rally Mulch Mat for weed control, treated pine sleepers, garden stakes, scoria and geotextile for drainage assistance.

We also carry items that you may require such as gardening tools (weeders, cultivators and trowels), pesticides, garden stakes, weed mat, lime and Dynamic Lifter.

No need to leave home as we deliver as little as 1/8 (0.125) of a cubic metre up to a full large truck full of product. We offer delivery to all surrounding suburbs such as Box Hill, Camberwell, Mont Albert and Balwyn. As a rough guide 1/8 (0.125) of a cubic metre is a large barrow worth of product.

If you would like help planning and calculating your mulch requirement feel free to contact us at the shop on 9890 3901 or utilise our helpful volume calculator on our website.

Happy gardening from the team at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies.

title: Our premium Mulch Products
excerpt: Applying a mulch to garden beds provides many benefits and can be applied year-round. Here are the benefits of mulching and a guide to the four mulches we carry.
bodyHtml:
Surrey Hills Mulch Products

Applying a mulch to garden beds provides many benefits and can be applied year-round. It’s a very cost-effective way to add or top up a covering to garden beds.

At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we can deliver bulk loads, small truck loads, 20kg bags or bring your ute or trailer to the yard to collect. There’s a useful calculator on our website that can assist you in calculating how much mulch you require.

Not only does applying a mulch aesthetically improve a garden but adding mulch to your garden provides many more benefits:

  • One of the biggest benefits mulches provide is adding nutrients to the soil and surrounding plants and improving soil structure;
  • Prevents loss of water due to natural evaporation;
  • Mulches are a perfect solution to suppress weed growth and used in conjunction with Weed Mat eliminates weed growth;
  • Reduces the amount of water required for the garden;
  • Decreases garden maintenance by reducing the amount of ‘weeding time’ the gardener must put into weeding;
  • In the cooler months it can help keep soil warmer so that plant growth is stimulated a little by providing a blanket-like effect;
  • Improves worm populations, and
  • Improves the visual aesthetics of gardens and landscapes.

Types of Mulch

Surrey Hills Garden Supplies carry 4 types of mulches: 10mm and 20mm Pine Bark Mulch, Midnight Black Mulch and Organic Mulch.

10mm Pine Bark

Chocolatey-brown nuggets in appearance. 10mm Pine Bark is a premium product choice for “high profile” landscaping works, particularly used in plant-scape areas aiming to contrast to existing buildings. It’s also known as Cottage Bark or Tan Bark. It’s renowned for its ability not to blow or wash away, but still allows airflow to the soil, as well as being excellent at water retention. It is long lasting and has good capacity to absorb and retain moisture. Installation should be to a depth of 100mm for new applications and typically 50-75mm for “top up” installations.

10mm pine mulch is great to spread under trees and shrubs where leaves and bark fall often as it will blend into the mulch. Pine Bark does not break down quickly. It’s also commonly used in playgrounds under playground equipment. It should be applied to the soil surface and not dug into the soil. It’s important to keep mulches away from the stems of plants to prevent mould or fungal disease in the bark.

20mm Pine Bark

20mm Pine Bark is a larger version of the Pine Bark and brown in appearance. 20mm Pine is generally used to cover larger open areas or larger garden beds. It’s also known as Tan Bark. It is renowned for its ability not to blow or wash away, but still allows air flow to the soil, as well as being excellent at water retention. It is long lasting, has good capacity to absorb and retain moisture, and is also extremely low maintenance. Installation should be to a depth of 100mm for new applications and typically 50-75mm for “top up” installations.

20mm pine mulch is great to spread under trees and shrubs where leaves and bark fall often as it will blend into the mulch. Pine Bark does not break down quickly. Due to its chunky appearance, it generally spreads further making it suitable for larger garden beds. It should be applied to the soil surface and not dug into the soil. It’s important to keep mulches away from the stems of plants to prevent mould or fungal disease in the bark.

Organic Mulch

Organic Mulch is an organic product, using a controlled batch composting technique. It’s also known as Compost or Compost Mulch. Organic Mulch is dark grey to almost black in appearance when moist. The blend comprises of soft garden organics, leaves and small branches that are mulched and aged until mature. Aged super fines, aged saw dust and Urea (nitrogen based additive) are also added to the blend.

Organic Mulch is great for increasing the level of organic matter for any type of soil, which in turn improves moisture retention, reduces soil erosion and gives slow release of nutrients into the soil. Organic Mulch creates an ideal environment for worms and micro-organisms.

Organic mulch is used in several landscaping applications such as domestic garden beds, new garden beds, vegetable patches, landscape projects and rose gardens, and is ideal for garden rejuvenation. A layer of 75mm – 100mm for new gardens and between 50mm – 75mm for existing gardens is recommended.

Black Midnight Mulch

Black Midnight Mulch is produced from recycled timber. The timber is produced in a grinder hammer mill free from any foreign materials as the product goes through a number of processes to remove foreign objects such as nails, staples and plastics. It is then put through a colour process using environmentally friendly products. The Longalife® coloured mulches have the added bonus of retaining colour for a substantially longer period than traditional mulches. It is recommended that coloured mulches are turned over with a shovel or pitchfork every 6 weeks. The Black Midnight Mulch is purely a decorative mulch and has no fertilising or organic properties.

Black Mulch should be applied to the soil surface and not dug into the soil. It’s important to keep mulches away from the stems of plants to prevent mould or fungal disease in the bark. A layer of 50mm – 100mm will give the best results for retaining moisture and preventing weed growth. It is recommended to wear gloves when spreading Black Mulch and to lay the bulk product on a tarp when it is delivered as it’s a dyed product and will stain.

title: What soil to use for a Vegetable Garden
excerpt: Have you ever thought about creating your own planter box or vegetable patch and which soil to use? We compare our Blended Soil and Premium Organic Soil for vegie patches.
bodyHtml:
What soil to use for a Vegetable Garden?

Have you ever thought about creating your own planter box or vegetable patch and which soil to use?

In these uncertain times of Covid19 with many restrictions in place, now is a great time to create or revitalise your vegie patch or planter box. There can be a lot of satisfaction for you and the kids watching a seedling sprout, watching it grow, nurturing it and ultimately picking your harvest and combining it with a home-cooked meal. The taste and freshness of your own vegetables is second to none.

With surrounding suburbs such as Camberwell, Balwyn, Canterbury and Box Hill having larger backyards there is often ample room to create a vegie patch.

At Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, we carry 2 types of soil that can be used for vegie patches.

Blended Soil

Our Blended Soil is a high-quality soil comprising a blend of several ingredients – sawdust, sandy loam, chicken manure and pine fines. Blended Soil is the ideal soil for planter boxes and vegetable gardens.

Premium Organic Soil

If you are looking for a soil that is less dense than Blended Soil and has a higher nutritional value then Premium Organic Soil is the ideal choice. Premium Organic Soil is a well aerated organic product which is a 50% mix of Organic Mulch and Blended Soil. It’s great for increasing the level of organic matter in the soil, which in turn improves moisture retention, reduces soil erosion and gives slow release of nutrients into the soil. Premium Organic Soil has more body than Organic Mulch as it has a higher percentage of soil.

In addition to our soils at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies, you can also enhance the soil by adding products such as Dynamic Lifter, manures and fertilisers such as Charlie Carp.

Other products that are used in vegie patches that we carry are Rally Mulch Mat for weed control, treated pine sleepers, pea straw, garden stakes, scoria and geotextile for drainage assistance.

Some other aspects to consider when commencing a vegie patch or planter box are how much sun the area will get during the day, the distance from the house (try and keep it as close as possible to your house) and that you will need to check its progress every day and water it.

Ideally choose an area with full sun for the majority of the day. Endeavour to create a well-drained vegie patch – either of our soils are ideally suited for growing Autumn vegetables such as lettuce, broccoli, onions and peas which all grow well in Melbourne.

We also carry items that you may require such as gardening tools (weeders, cultivators and trowels), pesticides, garden stakes, weed mat, lime and Dynamic Lifter.

No need to leave home as we deliver as little as 1/8 (0.125) of a cubic metre up to a full large truck full of product. We deliver to all surrounding suburbs such as Box Hill, Blackburn, Camberwell, Mont Albert and Balwyn.

If you would like help planning your vegetable garden or planter box, feel free to contact us at the shop on 9890 3901.

Happy gardening from the team at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies.

title: How to have a low Maintenance garden
excerpt: In the hustle and bustle of modern life, your garden is often what suffers. Taking it one small step at a time and breaking your garden into sections makes the task manageable and enjoyable.
bodyHtml:
How to have a low maintenance garden

In this day and age of hustle and bustle, getting the kids from one activity to another, trying to catch up with family and friends, one thing that suffers is your garden. To make it worse, you feel guilty for not having the time to get out and keep everything looking neat and tidy; the lawn is overgrown, weeds are popping up everywhere and the trees and plants are in desperate need of a good pruning. “Where do I start?” is the thing that keeps repeating itself in your mind. Taking it one small step at a time, breaking your garden into sections, will make the task less daunting and more manageable and enjoyable.

Firstly, your lawn needs to be mowed. Adjust your mower to the highest setting, this will make the grass more drought-tolerant (therefore less watering) and weeds will struggle to grow as there isn’t as much sunlight or water for them to feed on. Incorporate your grass clippings back over your lawn providing essential nutrients back into your lawn – the bonus of this is you do not have to rake and dispose of the grass clippings saving you precious time. Alternatively, you can replace some or all of the lawn with Lilydale Toppings or brick paving to eliminate mowing all together.

The next step, the job we all love to hate – weeding. If you have a small area, pulling the weeds out by hand is the most effective way to get the weeds, roots and all, out. For larger areas, using a product such as Round Up will work well and is generally easy to apply. If you weed regularly, the task will not be as time-consuming as it sounds. Remember to mulch your garden beds once all the weeds have died off, so as not to undo all the good work you have just done. Mulch provides moisture back into the soil and prevents any weeds from growing again.

No matter how therapeutic and relaxing watering your garden can be, in our busy lives we don’t have the time to do it as often and as long as it needs. Installing an automatic drip irrigation system can be the answer, with a timer attached you can set and forget it and your plants will still have all the water they require. The bonus of a system like this, in extremely hot weather, you don’t have to be up very early to beat the heat of the day or out in the garden late at night getting bitten by mosquitos.

Placing the right types of plants in the right spots in the garden can reduce the amount of time you need to tend to them. Plants that need little care, such as natives, can be very forgiving for a ‘lack’ of attention or water.

With some careful planning and a bit of foresight, your garden can be a stress-free wonderful haven, which you can enjoy rather than feeling guilty about all the work that needs to be done.

The staff at Surrey Hills Garden Supplies are more than willing to help with any questions you may have.
